types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business, government department, or charity. Also called Company, Institution, Agency, Firm, Body. Examples: Google, European Union, Rival Companies, Large Tech Companies.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Organization perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: MonetaryAmount: A quantity of money, often specified with a currency. Also called Sum, Value, Financial amount, Currency, Funds. Examples: €890m, £759m, €460m, €430m fine.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of MonetaryAmount perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

types.embedding_query_text: SoftwareService: A software application or platform provided to users, often over the internet. Also called Application, Platform, Digital service, Online tool, App. Examples: Google's own apps and services, its own apps and services, its own services.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareService
chosen_type.definition: An intangible offering provided to users through a software application or platform.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type captures the specific concept of a 'SoftwareService' as an intangible offering delivered via software. Service is the closest parent.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: WebApplication
candidates.comment: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: WebAPI
candidates.comment: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.

types.embedding_query_text: Law: A system of rules that a particular country or community recognizes as regulating the actions of its members and may enforce by the imposition of penalties. Also called Legislation, Statute, Act, Regulation, Code. Examples: Digital Markets Act, DMA, a landmark law, the regulations.

chosen_type.label: Legislation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Legislation includes 'law' and 'act', which directly matches the OIE_TYPE and the example 'Digital Markets Act'.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Principle, Theory, Abstraction. Examples: Consumer Choice, Unfair Advantage, Competition, Regulatory Credibility.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type adequately represents a general abstract idea or notion. Intangible is the most appropriate parent for an abstract concept.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: OfferItemCondition
candidates.comment: OfferItemCondition is an enumeration listing possible conditions for an item being offered. Also called item state, product condition, quality status. Examples: NewCondition, UsedCondition, RefurbishedCondition, DamagedCondition. Distinct from OfferShippingDetails, which describes shipping logistics.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

types.embedding_query_text: Regulation: A rule or directive made and maintained by an authority. Also called Rule, Directive, Ordinance, Statute, Guideline. Examples: EU's requirements, Play Store rules.

chosen_type.label: Legislation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Legislation explicitly includes 'regulation' and fits the examples 'EU's requirements' and 'Play Store rules'.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

types.embedding_query_text: CustomerGroup: A segment of individuals or organizations that purchase goods or services. Also called Clientele, Consumers, Market segment, User base, Patrons. Examples: European Customers, millions of European customers.

chosen_type.label: PeopleAudience
chosen_type.justification: PeopleAudience specifically describes characteristics of people, which fits 'CustomerGroup' and the example 'European Customers' better than the broader Audience.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman, Figure. Examples: Kent Walker, Teresa Ribera, Henna Virkkunen, Zach Meyers.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Person perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

types.embedding_query_text: SoftwareFeature: A distinct characteristic or capability of a software product or service. Also called Functionality, Capability, Aspect, Element, Component. Examples: Real-time Search features, Instant pricing, Direct availability for hotels, flights and restaurants, Safety protections on Google Play.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareFeature
chosen_type.definition: A distinct characteristic or capability of a software product or service.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a 'SoftwareFeature'. Intangible is a suitable parent for an abstract characteristic.

mentions: Direct availability for hotels, flights and restaurants

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

types.embedding_query_text: SoftwarePlatform: A foundational software system or environment upon which other applications can be built or run. Also called Operating system, Framework, Ecosystem, Environment, System. Examples: Google Play, Google's own marketplace.

chosen_type.label: RuntimePlatform
chosen_type.justification: RuntimePlatform describes a specialized software environment for executing programs, which accurately fits the definition of 'SoftwarePlatform' and the example 'Google Play'.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: InstallAction
candidates.comment: An InstallAction is a consume action representing the act of installing an application or software. Also called set up action, deploy action, load software. Examples: installing a new app on a phone, setting up an operating system, deploying a server application.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

types.embedding_query_text: OfficialGroup: A body of individuals holding official positions or authority. Also called Authority, Committee, Panel, Delegation, Bureau. Examples: EU Officials, regulators.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: GovernmentOrganization represents an organization that is part of a governmental body, which fits 'OfficialGroup' and the example 'EU Officials'.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalViolation: An act that breaks a law or rule. Also called Infringement, Breach, Offense, Transgression, Misconduct. Examples: DMA Breaches, abusing its power, two separate breaches of the DMA.

chosen_type.label: LegalViolation
chosen_type.definition: An act that breaks a law or rule.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a 'LegalViolation'. It is an action that constitutes a breach of law, making Action a suitable parent.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: CheckInAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent communicating their arrival and confirming a previously reserved service or place. Also called register arrival, confirm reservation, sign in. Examples: Checking into a hotel, checking in for a flight, checking in at a conference. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is simply arriving without prior reservation confirmation.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

types.embedding_query_text: BusinessPractice: A method or procedure used by a business in its operations. Also called Business method, Operational procedure, Commercial activity, Trade practice, Company policy. Examples: Google's Booking Service Practices, Google's practices, Google favoured its own services for helping people book flights and hotels over competitors in search results.

chosen_type.label: BusinessPractice
chosen_type.definition: A method or procedure used by a business in its operations.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a 'BusinessPractice'. It is an abstract method or procedure, making Intangible a suitable parent.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

types.embedding_query_text: CommercialOffer: A proposal to sell goods or services, often at a specific price. Also called Deal, Promotion, Discount, Proposal, Bargain. Examples: Cheaper offers, cheaper offers available outside Google's own marketplace.

chosen_type.label: OfferForPurchase
chosen_type.justification: OfferForPurchase specifically represents a proposal to sell something, which aligns perfectly with 'CommercialOffer' and the example 'Cheaper offers'.

candidates.label: AggregateOffer
candidates.comment: An AggregateOffer is an Offer that groups multiple individual offers for the same product or service, often from different merchants. Also called bundled offers, collective offer, multiple offers. Examples: A product page showing prices from several retailers, a flight search result listing different airline prices, a comparison shopping result. Distinct from Offer, which represents a single offer for a product or service.

candidates.label: OfferForPurchase
candidates.comment: An OfferForPurchase, as an Offer, represents a proposal to sell something. Also called sales offer, purchase offer, buy offer. Examples: an offer to sell a house, a product listing on an e-commerce site, a stock offering. Distinct from OfferForLease, which is an offer to rent.

candidates.label: Offer
candidates.comment: An Offer is an intangible entity representing a proposal to transfer rights to an item or provide a service. Also called proposal, deal, listing. Examples: an offer to sell a product, a rental agreement for an apartment, a service quote for car repair. Distinct from Order, which is a confirmation of an accepted offer.

candidates.label: OfferForLease
candidates.comment: An OfferForLease, as an Offer, represents a proposal to lease out something. Also called lease offer, rental offer, tenancy proposal. Examples: an offer to lease an apartment, a car lease deal, equipment rental terms. Distinct from OfferForPurchase, which is an offer to sell.

candidates.label: OfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An OfferCatalog is an ItemList containing related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs from the same provider. Also called product catalog, service catalog, sales brochure. Examples: an online store's product categories, a printed catalog of items for sale, a menu of services. Distinct from ItemList, which is a general list of items.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalHistory: The record of past legal actions, disputes, or proceedings involving an entity. Also called Legal record, Judicial background, Case history, Litigation history, Legal track record. Examples: Disputes with European regulators, long history of disputes with European regulators.

chosen_type.label: LegalHistory
chosen_type.definition: The record of past legal actions, disputes, or proceedings involving an entity.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents 'LegalHistory'. It is an abstract concept or record, making Intangible a suitable parent.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: LegislationObject
candidates.comment: A LegislationObject is a specific file or object containing a Legislation, which can exist in multiple formats. Also called legal document file, legislation artifact, law document. Examples: a PDF of a specific law, an HTML version of a regulation, a digitally signed legal document. Distinct from Legislation, which is the abstract legal document itself.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalCase: A dispute between opposing parties that may be resolved by a court or other legal process. Also called Lawsuit, Litigation, Court case, Legal action, Judicial proceeding. Examples: Competition cases, separate competition cases.

chosen_type.label: LegalCase
chosen_type.definition: A dispute between opposing parties that may be resolved by a court or other legal process.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a 'LegalCase'. It is a type of proceeding or happening, making Event a suitable parent.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: Courthouse
candidates.comment: A Courthouse is a government building where legal cases are heard and judicial proceedings take place. Also called court building, hall of justice, judicial building. Examples: Supreme Court of the United States, Old Bailey, local county courthouse.

candidates.label: TieAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

types.embedding_query_text: ProductAttribute: A characteristic or quality of a product. Also called Feature, Characteristic, Property, Quality, Trait. Examples: Product Quality, the quality of their products.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: PropertyValue represents a property-value pair or feature, which fits 'ProductAttribute' and the example 'Product Quality'.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

types.embedding_query_text: BusinessAttribute: A characteristic or quality pertaining to a business entity or its operations. Also called Business characteristic, Company trait, Market characteristic, Operational aspect, Commercial feature. Examples: Market Position.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: PropertyValue represents a property-value pair or feature, which fits 'BusinessAttribute' and the example 'Market Position'.

candidates.label: BusinessFunction
candidates.comment: A BusinessFunction is an Enumeration specifying the type of activity or access rights offered by an organization through an offer. Also called commercial activity, service type, transaction type. Examples: Sell, LeaseOut, Repair, ProvideService, Buy.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: BusinessAudience
candidates.comment: A BusinessAudience is an Audience defined by characteristics relevant to businesses, such as their industry, size, or role in the value chain. Also called B2B audience, corporate audience, professional audience. Examples: small business owners, IT managers, marketing executives, manufacturing companies. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which targets individual consumers.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

types.embedding_query_text: Product: An article or substance that is manufactured or refined for sale. Also called Good, Merchandise, Item, Commodity, Offering. Examples: Best Products.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Product perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

types.embedding_query_text: Position: A job or role within an organization. Also called Role, Title, Job, Office, Post. Examples: Director of Research.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: OrganizationRole describes a specific function or position within an organization, which perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and the example 'Director of Research'.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: JobPosting
candidates.comment: A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening. Examples: a software engineer job posting, a marketing manager vacancy, a retail associate opening.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A happening or occurrence, especially one of importance. Also called Occurrence, Incident, Happening, Affair, Development. Examples: Delay in decision finalization, a delay in the competition authority finalising its decision against Google.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Event perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

types.embedding_query_text: InternationalRelations: The political, economic, and social interactions between different countries. Also called Foreign relations, Diplomacy, Global affairs, International affairs, Cross-border ties. Examples: EU-US relations.

chosen_type.label: InternationalRelations
chosen_type.definition: The political, economic, and social interactions between different countries.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents 'InternationalRelations'. It is an abstract concept or relationship, making Intangible a suitable parent.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: Trip
candidates.comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.

candidates.label: CurrencyConversionService
candidates.comment: A CurrencyConversionService is a financial service that facilitates the exchange of funds from one currency to another. Also called foreign exchange service, money exchange, currency exchange. Examples: A bank's foreign exchange desk, an online currency converter, a travel money service.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a temporary, seasonal modification to a standard merchant return policy. Also called holiday return policy, seasonal return exception, extended return period. Examples: "extended holiday return window", "special return policy for Black Friday purchases".

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

types.embedding_query_text: EconomicPolicy: A course of action taken by a government to influence the economy. Also called Fiscal policy, Monetary policy, Trade policy, Financial strategy, Economic measure. Examples: New tariffs.

chosen_type.label: EconomicPolicy
chosen_type.definition: A course of action taken by a government to influence the economy.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents 'EconomicPolicy'. It is an abstract plan or course of action, making Intangible a suitable parent.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: BoardingPolicyType
candidates.comment: An Enumeration representing different policies used by airlines for boarding passengers. Also called airline boarding rule, boarding group type, flight boarding policy. Examples: "Zone boarding", "Group boarding", "Priority boarding", "Family boarding".

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a temporary, seasonal modification to a standard merchant return policy. Also called holiday return policy, seasonal return exception, extended return period. Examples: "extended holiday return window", "special return policy for Black Friday purchases".

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

types.embedding_query_text: Action: The process of doing something, typically to achieve an aim. Also called Deed, Act, Measure, Initiative, Undertaking. Examples: EU's efforts, its efforts.

chosen_type.label: Action
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Action perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

candidates.label: WantAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a desire or wish for an object or outcome. Also called desire, wish for, covet. Examples: wanting a new car, desiring a specific job, wishing for peace.

candidates.label: Action
candidates.comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

types.embedding_query_text: Trait: A distinguishing quality or characteristic, typically one belonging to a person. Also called Characteristic, Quality, Feature, Attribute, Aspect. Examples: US president's unpredictability, Unwillingness to comply with deals, unwillingness to comply with his own deals.

chosen_type.label: Property
chosen_type.justification: Property represents an attribute or characteristic, which aligns well with the abstract concept of a 'Trait' and its examples.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: ParentAudience
candidates.comment: A ParentAudience, as a PeopleAudience, describes characteristics of parents who might be interested in certain content. Also called parental demographic, parent group, family audience. Examples: 'parents of young children', 'parents of teenagers', 'expectant parents'. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which is a broader category for any group of people.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Strategy: A plan of action or policy designed to achieve a major or overall aim. Also called Plan, Approach, Tactic, Method, Policy. Examples: Treading Softly.

chosen_type.label: Strategy
chosen_type.definition: A plan of action or policy designed to achieve a major or overall aim.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a 'Strategy'. It is an abstract plan, making Intangible a suitable parent.

candidates.label: ScheduleAction
candidates.comment: The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking. Examples: scheduling a doctor's appointment, booking a meeting room, planning a project timeline, arranging a delivery. Distinct from ReserveAction, which implies making a reservation for a specific resource or service.

candidates.label: TieAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.

candidates.label: PlanAction
candidates.comment: PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging. Examples: planning a wedding, scheduling a meeting, arranging a trip itinerary, setting up a project timeline.

candidates.label: ChooseAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.

candidates.label: Diet
candidates.comment: A creative work outlining a strategy for regulating food intake to achieve a specific health or fitness goal. Also called Eating plan, nutritional regimen, dietary program, meal plan. Examples: The Mediterranean diet, a ketogenic diet, a low-sodium diet, a vegan diet. Distinct from NutritionInformation, which provides factual data about food content.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Span, Term, Interval, Length. Examples: 60 days.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org definition of Duration perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: LegalBody: An official organization or group with legal authority, such as a court. Also called Judicial body, Legal institution, Tribunal, Judiciary, Court system. Examples: Court.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: GovernmentOrganization represents an organization that is part of a governmental body, which fits 'LegalBody' and the example 'Court'.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, specified by number, month, and year. Also called Day, Calendar date, Specific day, Point in time, Moment. Examples: 24/07/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org datatype Date perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.
